The Cradle Blueprint had long been completed, but Crow hesitated for a long time about where to store it.
Originally, he hid it in a secret compartment in his study, only for it to be accidentally discovered by three Disciples. The most troublesome one kept asking when the mountains would be connected by cradles.
Though cradles were easy to make, they required sturdier tracks and swifter flowing water to match. In the mountains now, ever since his senior brother stopped inquiring about mechanisms, no one could replicate the flowing water tracks.
So he hid the blueprint in a stone chamber, looking at it again and again... until he finally decided to fold it into a paper kite.
But just as he was about to hang it up, he hesitated once more. He unfolded the kite, wrote a long letter, and then folded it back.
After hanging it, Crow gazed at the circling paper kites above and smiled. Would it be as he predicted—his senior brother discovering The Secret first—or would one of the children in these little kites find it first?
